A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the yeast strain used in our study, Y-2461, is not suitable for use in a process that requires a high yield of ethanol from d-xyloses.
pentose fermentation by Pachysolen is not limited by oxygen availability and that the use of azide as an inhibitor of respiration is not a viable approach for improving pentose conversion.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the pentose pathway in P. tannophilus is highly regulated and that the addition of respiratory inhibitors does not necessarily improve ethanol production.
azide is a potent inhibitor of P. tannophilus growth and metabolism and that the use of azide to improve pentose fermentation is unlikely.
